english: A circle with centre $C(-12,0)$ cuts the parabola $y^{2}=12x$ orthogonally. Then the radius of the circle is
hindi: केन्द्र $C(-12,0)$ वाला एक वृत्त परवलय $y^{2}=12x$ को लम्बकोणीय रूप से (orthogonally) काटता है। तब वृत्त की त्रिज्या है
solution: At a common point $P$, the circle's tangent is perpendicular to the radius $CP$; orthogonality means it is also perpendicular to the parabola's tangent, so $CP$ lies along the tangent to the parabola at $P$.
Check: $(x+12)^{2}+12x=720\Rightarrow x^{2}+36x-576=0\Rightarrow x=12$ ($x=-48$ rejected), so the circle meets the parabola only at $(12,\pm12)$, orthogonally at both.
solution_full: Let the circle meet the parabola at $P$. The tangent to the circle at $P$ is perpendicular to the radius $CP$.

The curves cut orthogonally at $P$, so the tangent to the circle at $P$ is perpendicular to the tangent to the parabola at $P$. Two lines through $P$ perpendicular to the same line coincide, hence the line $CP$ is the tangent to the parabola at $P$.
For $y^{2}=12x$ we have $a=3$, so $P=(3t^{2},6t)$ and the tangent at $P$ is $ty=x+3t^{2}$.
This tangent passes through $C(-12,0)$: $0=-12+3t^{2}$, so $t^{2}=4$, $t=\pm2$, and $P=(12,\pm12)$.

Check that the configuration is consistent: the circle $(x+12)^{2}+y^{2}=720$ meets $y^{2}=12x$ where $x^{2}+24x+144+12x=720$, i.e. $x^{2}+36x-576=0$, i.e. $(x-12)(x+48)=0$. Since $x\geq0$ on the parabola, $x=12$, giving only $(12,12)$ and $(12,-12)$, and at both the slope of $CP$ ($\pm\frac{1}{2}$) equals the slope of the parabola's tangent ($\frac{6}{y}=\pm\frac{1}{2}$).
originality_note: New: a circle centred on the axis behind the vertex cuts the parabola orthogonally exactly where the parabola's tangent passes through the centre (way 3, an object fixed by an orthogonality condition). Closest known: 'curves x = y^2 and xy = k cut orthogonally' and the JEE Main 2018 problem on the circle through P and the axis intercepts of the tangent and normal at P. Different because: the second curve is a circle with unknown radius, and orthogonality turns into the tangent of the parabola passing through a given point.

concept_use.Tangent to the parabola: point, slope an: The tangent at P(3t^2, 6t) in parametric form, ty = x + 3t^2, is made to pass through C(-12, 0).
concept_use.Angle of intersection between two curves: Orthogonal intersection is converted into: the radius CP is along the parabola's tangent at P, since the circle's tangent there is perpendicular to both.

stem_review: Read as a student: every curve and point is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy and checked by an independent numerical route, is unique and matches the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked that such a circle exists and is unique (t^2 = 4 only), that it meets the parabola only at (12, ±12) and orthogonally at both, and that (A) 12 sqrt5 is the only correct option. Changed: an earlier design (circle centred at the focus) was replaced because its core matched a published JEE Main problem.
key_step: Turning orthogonality into 'the parabola's tangent at P passes through the centre', then the parametric tangent.
justification: A short chain of three routine steps (orthogonality condition, parametric tangent through a point, distance) with no real insight. Same kind of demand as 2026-P2-Q17 (L2, angle between tangents of two conics) and 2026-P2-Q2 (L2).
